title: Preservation in the open and finite etale cases
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,V$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and let $f:V\to X$ be an open immersion or a finite etale morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work with the ordinary derived categories of constant-coefficient module sheaves on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $Rf_A^{\times}$ for the right adjoint to extension by zero $f_!$ in the open case and to $Rf_!=f_*$ in the finite etale case, as in [prop-exc-open-adjoint, prop-exc-finite-etale-adjoint].

For all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
 Rf_A^{\times}D_c^{[a,b]}(X,A)\subseteq D_c^{[a,b]}(V,A),
$$
where $D_c^{[a,b]}$ is the constructible cohomological interval [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. For integers $c\leq d$, if $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then $Rf_A^{\times}K$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[c,d]$.

For each quotient $A\to B=A_{E,m}$ with $1\leq m\leq n$ and each $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the derived coefficient comparison is an isomorphism in $D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$:
$$
 (Rf_A^{\times}K)\otimes_A^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}
 Rf_B^{\times}(K\otimes_A^L B).
$$
Here derived coefficient extension is [def-weil-derived-tensor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; the comparison is the derived inverse-image coefficient comparison under the adjunction identifications $Rf_A^{\times}\cong f_A^*$ and $Rf_B^{\times}\cong f_B^*$. If $K$ is bounded constructible and has finite Tor amplitude, both sides are bounded constructible over $B$ and retain its Tor-amplitude interval. All interval bounds are independent of $n$ and $m$.

proof.text: By [prop-exc-open-adjoint] in the open case, and [prop-exc-finite-etale-adjoint] in the finite etale case, the relevant compact-support functor has $f^*$ as its right adjoint on the entire ordinary derived categories. Identify $Rf^{\times}$ with this right adjoint, using the isomorphism characterized by the adjunction bijections. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], $f_A^*$ is exact for every finite coefficient ring $A$, and likewise for $B$. Thus it can be applied termwise to any complex: exactness preserves cycles, boundaries and their quotients, so $\mathcal H^q(f_A^*K)=f_A^*\mathcal H^q(K)$, and it preserves quasi-isomorphisms. This reduces the interval assertions to constructibility of the inverse image and the Tor assertion to a flat-complex calculation.

proof.text: Let $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[c,d]$. Apply the pro-etale assertion of [lem-sf-flat-model] to obtain a complex $P\simeq K$ of flat $A_X$-module sheaves supported in $[c,d]$. That statement permits any scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible; its auxiliary finite-field coefficient convention imposes no $k$-scheme hypothesis on $X$. The morphism of ringed topoi in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with its constant-ring structure isomorphism, meets the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback]. Hence every term of $f_A^*P$ is flat over $A_V$, and it vanishes outside $[c,d]$. It represents $f_A^*K$ by step 1. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For every $A_V$-module sheaf $M$ in degree zero, [def-weil-derived-tensor] computes $f_A^*K\otimes_A^L M$ by $(f_A^*P)\otimes_A M$, whose terms outside $[c,d]$ are zero. Its cohomology there is therefore zero. This is precisely the Tor bound, also for module sheaves $M$ not pulled back from $X$.

proof.text: For the coefficient comparison let $K$ now be any derived complex. Choose $P\to K$ K-flat with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Step 1 shows that $f_A^*P$ represents $f_A^*K$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] shows it is K-flat with flat terms. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the left side of the requested comparison is represented, as a complex of $B_V$-modules, by $(f_A^*P)\otimes_{A_V}B_V$. The right side is represented by $f_B^*(P\otimes_{A_X}B_X)$, since $P\otimes_{A_X}B_X$ represents the coefficient extension and $f_B^*$ is exact. The ordinary tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and the identification $f^{-1}B_X=B_V$ from [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] give an isomorphism between these complexes. Concretely both identify to $f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}A_X}B_V$, and the map is the identity on local pure tensors $p\otimes b$. It is $B_V$-linear, respects differentials, and is natural in $P$. The resolution independence in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes this the derived comparison specified in the statement, hence an isomorphism for arbitrary $K$. This calculation uses no flatness of $A\to B$.

It remains to justify bounded constructibility after reduction, rather than infer it from a nonflat quotient. Suppose $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ has Tor amplitude $[c,d]$. The constant $A$-module sheaf $B_X$ is bounded constructible in degree zero, since $B$ is a finite $A$-module. Apply [lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology] to $K$ and $B_X$: all cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes_A^L B$ are constructible as $A$-module sheaves. Its cohomology vanishes outside $[c,d]$ by the defining Tor test [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with $M=B_X$. These cohomology sheaves are also constructible as $B$-module sheaves: their $A$-action factors through $B=A/I$. On a trivializing covering member write such a cohomology sheaf as $F\cong\underline M$. Taking the quotient by $I$ gives $F=F/IF\cong\underline{M/IM}$: sheafification of the constant presheaf commutes with the cokernel defining this quotient. The finite module $M/IM$ is a $B$-module, and this quotient isomorphism is $B$-linear. This also works on empty covering members, without asserting that an arbitrary label $M$ there is annihilated by $I$. Thus reduction is bounded constructible over $B$. The model $P$ of step 3 reduces to $P\otimes_A B$, a bounded flat $B$-complex in $[c,d]$, by [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model]. Hence it also retains Tor amplitude $[c,d]$. Apply steps 2 and 3 with coefficients $B$ to get the same assertions for $Rf_B^{\times}(K\otimes_A^L B)$; step 4 gives them for the isomorphic left side. All complexes used for the bounds are supported in the original intervals, so the constants do not depend on either coefficient exponent.
